numerical_characteristics.magnitude: int64.min (the NaT sentinel) for integer-encoded time arrays; float NaN for float-encoded arrays
category_specific_evidence: Integer arrays encode NaT as int64.min (numpy/pandas NaT bit pattern); float arrays encode NaT as NaN (from _decode_to_timedelta comment in discussion diff)
In numpy >= 2.5 (numpy/numpy#31378) int64.min * timedelta64 raises OverflowError instead of silently producing NaT (PR#11340 and commit message)
Fix: detect the int64.min sentinel (integer dtype) and float NaN before multiplication and return np.timedelta64('NaT', unit)
Values above int64.max or below int64.min raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta
Previously the CF decode path relied on silent NaT and surfaced as ValueError: unable to decode time units through decode_cf
Old code had 'on windows multiplying nan leads to RuntimeWarning' suppression for invalid value in multiply
Old uint dtype overflow check (value.dtype.kind == 'u' and not np.int64(delta) == value) was replaced by the new path
Regression coverage relies on existing int64.min parametrizations of test_cf_timedelta and test_roundtrip_timedelta64_nanosecond_precision
Test parametrize datetime64 values were pinned to ns unit because numpy >= 2.5 deprecates generic unit datetime64/timedelta64
reproduction_risks: Reproduction requires numpy >= 2.5 for the OverflowError path; older numpy silently produces NaT for int64.min * timedelta64
Generic (unitless) datetime64/timedelta64 construction emits DeprecationWarning in numpy >= 2.5, which can abort collection under filterwarnings=error
Windows may emit RuntimeWarning on NaN multiplication in the old code path
The uint64 overflow handling was changed, so reproduction should not assume the old uint check remains
